findings.text: Tier object holds two intrusive lists for global ordering and member types, an integer start of its abstract distance window, an embedded device object, and a node mask aggregating members of all lower tiers.

Per node demotion state is a single preferred destination mask. Per node type association pairs a pointer to a device type descriptor with a count of how many devices currently map that node to that type.

A dedicated mutex serializes tier creation, node to tier assignment, demotion table rebuilds, type map updates and sysfs mask reads. Several helpers require the caller to already hold it and assert that ownership.

Default DRAM performance reference data is guarded by its own mutex. The per node pointer to its tier is published with RCU semantics, read under RCU in query paths and cleared with a grace period before the underlying tier storage is recycled.
Predicate reports whether a folio should use access time tracking for tiering. It is true only when tiering is enabled in the balancing mode controls and the folio node is not classified as top tier.

Query classifies a node as top tier when it has no NUMA descriptor, when it has no assigned tier object, or when its tier start distance does not exceed a global threshold. Otherwise it reports non top tier.

Allocator creates a type descriptor with given distance, empty membership and fresh reference count. Finder returns an existing entry with matching distance or allocates and links a new one. Release drops a reference and frees at last put, and bulk helper unlinks and releases a whole list.

Node to type binding increments a per node map count and takes a type reference only on first mapping to that type. Unbinding decrements, and when the count reaches zero it clears the association and releases the reference. Both paths hold the tier mutex.
Distance calculation delegates to a blocking notification chain keyed by node with an integer accumulator. Registration helpers add or remove algorithm callbacks from that chain.

One helper records reference DRAM latency and bandwidth from the first reporting node and rejects later reports that deviate by ten percent or more on any component. A second helper scales a base distance by relative total latency and inverse relative total bandwidth.

Compressed pool accounting exposes current usage as a flushed byte counter, a tunable maximum accepting numeric or maximum keyword and updated atomically, and a writeback toggle accepting only zero or one with single store semantics. Current and maximum are hidden on the root cgroup.

Subsystem initialization no-ops when the controller is disabled, otherwise registers swap controls unconditionally and compressed pool controls only when that feature is compiled in, warning on registration failure but still reporting success.

Tiers are ordered by quantized distance start. Lookup rounds the requested distance down to chunk granularity, reuses a tier with equal start, otherwise allocates and inserts a new tier in sorted position and publishes a device whose numeric identity derives from the start value.

For each populated tier except the last, the rebuild scans only nodes of the immediately lower tier, skipping all other memory nodes, and retains every candidate at the minimal distance from the source, so equidistant targets form a selection set for later random choice.

Threshold for top tier is set from the highest tier whose nodes intersect the CPU populated set, using its window maximum. Fallback masks are then built by sweeping tiers in order and successively removing each tier nodes, leaving only strictly lower tiers in each mask.

Assigning a node validates that it has memory, refreshes its distance through the algorithm chain, falls back to default DRAM type on allocation failure, records membership, ensures a tier exists, and publishes the tier pointer. Preconfigured nodes keep their existing type.

A node leaves a tier by clearing the published pointer, waiting for readers, removing itself from type membership, unlinking the type when empty, and destroying the tier device when its member list becomes empty. Unregister drives asynchronous release that frees the tier storage.

Boot registers a tier bus, allocates per node demotion storage when migration is enabled, creates a default DRAM type and records DRAM backed CPU nodes, then subscribes to memory hotplug. Hotplug removal clears the tier and rebuilds targets, addition assigns a tier and rebuilds targets.

Rebuild is a no-op when demotion storage is absent or when compiled without migration support. Otherwise it first blanks all preferred and fallback state with a grace period, then repopulates preferred sets, threshold and fallback masks, and finally logs the resulting tables.

User interface comprises compressed pool files under each non root memory cgroup and a per tier read only node list attribute. The latter snapshots the union of member type masks under lock and formats it as a list.

Late boot holds online memory protection and the tier mutex while assigning every memory node that lacks a type, ignoring individual assignment failures, then performs one demotion rebuild before releasing protection.

Tier creation reports invalid input when an already linked type cannot find its quantized tier, no memory on allocation failure, and propagates device registration errors after unlinking and dropping the device reference. Distance helpers reject zero totals, missing reference and prior mismatch with distinct error codes.
Published names include three compressed pool control files and a tiering bus with per tier devices exposing a node list. Global demotion enable flag starts cleared.
